overall: The AG found the Brookline Advisory Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by not reviewing requested executive session minutes at its next meeting and by failing to respond to the request within 10 days; only future compliance was ordered.

allegations.summary: Requested executive session minutes covering a settlement approval, but the committee did not review them at its next meetings and instead waited about a month.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law where it did not review the minutes at the next available meeting but instead waited until April 24.

allegations.summary: A request for executive session minutes received no response within 10 days; the committee responded only after the complaint was filed.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Committee did not do so, it violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to properly respond to a request for executive session minutes.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law (no further remedial action, since the committee had already reviewed the minutes and responded to the requester).
remedy_passage: We order the Committee’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
